title: Colorado AI Chatbot Disclosure Rulemaking — Timeline and Compliance (Council of AI, 2026-10-07)
context: 2026-10-07 EAT cycle — Council Signal tracks Colorado SB 24-205 (now effective Aug 1, 2026) and the Attorney General's implementing rulemaking. The disclosure obligations for AI chatbots interacting with Colorado residents are now live; the measurement question is whether deployers can prove disclosure was made, not just assert it.
body: Colorado's AI transparency law (SB 24-205, signed April 2024) imposed disclosure obligations on deployers of high-risk AI systems, with the chatbot-specific provisions taking effect August 1, 2026. The Attorney General's rulemaking process has produced implementing regulations that clarify what 'clear and conspicuous' disclosure means in practice and how deployers must document compliance. The key timeline: SB 24-205 signed April 2024; AG rulemaking draft released January 2025; public comment closed March 2025; final rules published June 2025; enforcement began August 1, 2026. The Council of AI's position is that the chatbot disclosure requirement is a measurement-surface obligation, not merely a UI requirement. A deployer must be able to prove — with signed, timestamped evidence — that every qualifying interaction included the required disclosure. Under the Council of AI framework, this maps to the verified measurement credential: the disclosure event (timestamp, interaction-ID, disclosure-method, content-delivered) is recorded, signed with Ed25519, and indexed in the Containment Index as a compliance observation. The AG's final rules require that disclosure be 'readily perceivable' and that deployers maintain records demonstrating compliance for three years. A static privacy-policy update does not satisfy this — the obligation attaches to each qualifying interaction, which means deployers need a continuous measurement and logging capability. The Council of AI's measurement board (14 axes) includes an operational-disclosure axis that tracks disclosure-fidelity: whether the disclosure was rendered, whether it was rendered before the AI interaction began, and whether the user's response indicated comprehension. These observations are signed and frozen in the board manifest, giving deployers a verifiable evidence stream rather than a self-attested checklist. For organisations deploying chatbots that interact with Colorado residents, the practical steps are: (1) instrument every qualifying interaction with a disclosure event; (2) sign each event with a verified measurement credential; (3) index the events in an append-only log (the Containment Index model); (4) make the log available for AG audit on request. This is monitored containment applied to state-level chatbot regulation — the disclosure claim is backed by a signed evidence chain, not by a policy document last reviewed at deployment time.
